Anterior thoracic wall abscess would show localized soft tissue swelling and fluid collection, but this is less likely without specific imaging findings. Anterior mediastinal lymphoma presents as a mass in the anterior mediastinum, potentially compressing adjacent structures, leading to symptoms like superior vena cava syndrome. Given the evidence and typical presentations, anterior mediastinal lymphoma is the most likely diagnosis due to its characteristic mass effect and symptomatology, supported by the highest probability in the reasoning chain.
